content:
Artificial intelligence data centers are being built on a massive scale across the United States, and they have already had a severe impact on the entire consumer electronics industry. The surge in bulk purchases of high-end HBM2 DRAM has completely reshaped the supply chain, making it extremely difficult to obtain consumer-grade memory and storage products.

Since the beginning of this year, SSD and DDR5 RAM prices have skyrocketed. Apple finally adjusted its pricing at the end of June—raising prices across all product lines by US$100 to over US$400. Despite the price increases, the company is still struggling to maintain MacBook Air inventory.

In June, Apple raised the MacBook Air price from US$1,099 to US$1,299, having previously bumped it slightly from US$999 to US$1,099 in March when the M5 model launched. Of course, Apple also doubled the base storage configuration from 256GB to 512GB, so for users who originally needed to purchase more storage space, this is effectively a net gain.

However, even with price hikes to offset rising memory and storage costs, Apple is still struggling to maintain M5 MacBook Air inventory—even though this is a relatively new computer.

According to Mark Gurman, if you try to order a MacBook Air from Apple right now, the earliest you can get your hands on one is at the end of the month, and the retail channel side describes MacBook Air supply as "the tightest they can remember."

Apple's recent "Back to School" promotional campaign also specifically notes that MacBook Air availability depends on stock—a rare occurrence for a mid-cycle product.

Reasons behind MacBook Air supply shortages

According to Gurman's sources, this shortage is due to the memory crisis, but also involves Apple prioritizing production of base model M5 MacBook Pro in preparation for updates this autumn. Excerpted from the "Power On" newsletter:

As far as I know, the MacBook Air shortage is indeed related to the ongoing memory crunch. Apple has been trying to alleviate the problem by preparing to source memory from Chinese suppliers, at least for products sold in China.

Overall, the coming years will be a challenging period for Apple. The company has warned that sales for the next quarter will be affected by supply constraints, and has also warned that further price hikes may be possible. We may see more Mac product price adjustments to balance demand.

Amazon currently has M5 MacBook Air in stock with next-day delivery and a US$100 discount. If you've been thinking about getting one, this may be your last chance before third-party channel conditions worsen.
